Newsletter.heading: Four houses, once a month
Newsletter.body: New properties, quiet seasons worth booking into, and the occasional rate drop. No more than one email a month, and never a shared list.

ValueProps.visitedBody: Someone from our team has stayed a night in each property on this site. If a house does not hold up in person, it does not go on the list.
ValueProps.onePriceBody: The number you see at checkout is the number you pay. Cleaning and service are itemised up front, and there are no resort fees waiting at the door.
ValueProps.hostsReplyBody: Our hosts reply in under two hours on average. Most of them live within walking distance and will meet you with the keys themselves.
ValueProps.specialistsBody: A travel specialist is available seven days a week to move dates, arrange transfers or find you a table that is fully booked online.

Testimonials.lindqvistQuote: We have booked four trips through Wanderstay now and not one of them has been a compromise. The houses are genuinely as described, which sounds like a low bar until you have used the alternatives.
Testimonials.lindqvistRole: Booked The Fjord Cabin and three others
Testimonials.haddadQuote: I moved our dates twice and changed the guest count once. Both times someone picked up within a minute and sorted it without a fee. That is the whole reason I keep coming back.
Testimonials.okonkwoQuote: The photography is honest. Nothing was shot with a lens that made a small room look enormous. What we walked into was exactly what we chose eight weeks earlier.

About.metaDescription: Wanderstay is a small team that visits every house before listing it. Here is how we choose properties, how we work with hosts, and who we are.
About.heading: We turn down four houses for every one we list
About.intro: Wanderstay is eleven people working out of Stockholm and Bologna. We are not trying to be the biggest travel site — we are trying to be the one where every house on the list is one we would send a friend to.
About.principlesIntro: There is no algorithm and no paid placement. There is a checklist, a night in the bed, and an argument afterwards.
About.stayBeforeListingBody: Someone from the team spends a night in every house. We check the shower pressure, the mattress, the noise at 7 AM and whether the kitchen has a decent knife. About four in five houses do not make it past this stage.
About.honestPhotographyTitle: We show the room, not the lens
About.honestPhotographyBody: Nothing is shot on a lens that makes a small room look like a hall. If a house has one difficult feature — two hundred steps, a sand road, an early ferry — it is written on the page in plain English rather than buried in the rules.
About.hostsNotInventoryTitle: We work with hosts, not inventory
About.hostsNotInventoryBody: Every property here is run by an individual or a family, not a management company. We pay hosts within 48 hours of check-in and we do not charge them for placement.
About.shortListBody: Forty-eight houses is a number we can hold in our heads. It means when you call and describe what you want, the person on the phone has been to the house they are recommending.
About.firstHouseTitle: One house on the Amalfi coast
About.firstHouseBody: Wanderstay began as a spreadsheet of houses two friends had stayed in and would vouch for. Casa Limone was the first, and it is still on the list.
About.twelveHousesBody: We started visiting properties properly rather than relying on recommendations, and turned down the first house that did not hold up in person.
About.specialistsBody: We hired the first full-time travel specialists so that someone with real knowledge of every property answers the phone seven days a week.
About.todayBody: The list is the largest it has ever been and the acceptance rate is the lowest it has ever been. We intend to keep it that way.
About.teamHeading: The people you will deal with
About.teamIntro: Eleven of us in total, four of whom you are most likely to speak to. Everyone on this list has stayed in at least a third of the houses on the site.
About.elinMeta: Founder · Visits about thirty houses a year
About.marcoMeta: Head of properties · Based in Bologna
About.nadiaMeta: Lead travel specialist · Speaks to most of you first
About.tomMeta: Host relations · Handles payouts and standards
About.hostBody: We read every application. Here is roughly what the process looks like and how long each stage takes.
About.hostStepApplication: You send photographs, the address and a paragraph about the house
About.hostStepReply: We reply within two weeks, either way
About.hostStepConversation: A conversation, usually about an hour, usually on the phone
About.hostStepVisit: One of us comes and stays a night, at our own cost
About.hostStepLive: If it is a yes, you are live within three weeks

Faq.metaDescription: Answers on booking, payment, cancellation, keys and house rules — plus how to reach a Wanderstay specialist seven days a week.
Faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
Faq.intro: {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} covering the things guests ask most often. If yours is not here, a specialist will answer it in under an hour.
Faq.bookingLeadTimeQuestion: How far in advance should I book?
Faq.bookingLeadTimeAnswer: For July and August in the Mediterranean, four to five months is realistic — the coastal houses go first. Northern Europe and the Alps are far more relaxed outside the ski season, and you can often book six weeks out. If the dates you want are gone, tell a specialist and we will let you know the moment something opens up.
Faq.afterReservingAnswer: Your dates are held immediately and your host has 24 hours to accept. Almost all of them accept within two hours. You will get a confirmation email with a booking reference as soon as they do, and your card is only charged at that point.
Faq.changingDatesQuestion: Can I change my dates after booking?
Faq.changingDatesAnswer: Yes, and there is no Wanderstay fee for doing it. Open the booking in My Trips and choose Request a change, or call a specialist. Date changes depend on the house being free, so the earlier you ask the better. If the new dates cost more, you pay the difference; if they cost less, we refund it.
Faq.minimumStayAnswer: Most houses ask for three nights, and a handful of the larger properties ask for seven in high season. The minimum is shown on the booking widget as soon as you pick a check-in date, so you will never get to checkout and be surprised by it.
Faq.whenCardChargedAnswer: Once your host accepts. Nothing is taken at the point you press Confirm and reserve — the amount is authorised, not captured. If your host declines or does not respond within 24 hours, the authorisation is released and you are charged nothing at all.
Faq.cancellationPolicyAnswer: Cancel more than 14 days before check-in and you get a full refund including all fees. Between 14 and 7 days, you are refunded half the accommodation cost and all fees. Inside 7 days the booking is non-refundable, because at that point the house cannot realistically be re-let. A few properties run stricter terms, and those are always stated on the house page before you book.
Faq.hiddenFeesQuestion: Are there any fees added later?
Faq.hiddenFeesAnswer: No. The total at checkout includes the nightly rate, the cleaning fee, our service fee and any local occupancy tax. There is nothing to pay on arrival unless you ask your host for something extra, like a cook or an airport transfer.
Faq.acceptedCardsAnswer: Visa, Mastercard and American Express. We do not currently take bank transfer for stays under $2,000, though a specialist can arrange it for longer bookings and multi-house trips.
Faq.collectingKeysQuestion: How do I get the keys?
Faq.collectingKeysAnswer: It depends on the house, and it is always written on your booking. Roughly two thirds of our hosts meet guests in person; the rest use a keypad or a lockbox and send you the code the night before you arrive. Either way you will know exactly what to expect before you travel.
Faq.problemOnArrivalQuestion: What if something is wrong when I arrive?
Faq.problemOnArrivalAnswer: Call the number on your booking confirmation. A specialist answers seven days a week and can reach your host directly. If a problem cannot be fixed the same day and it materially affects your stay, we will move you to a comparable house or refund the affected nights.
Faq.bringingADogAnswer: At some houses, yes. Look for Pets welcome in the amenity list, and give the host advance notice through the special requests box at checkout. Assistance dogs are welcome at every property on the site regardless of what the listing says.
Faq.choosingHousesQuestion: How do you choose the houses?
Faq.choosingHousesAnswer: Someone from our team stays a night in every property before it is listed, and we go back roughly every eighteen months. We turn down about four out of five houses that apply. Most of the time the reason is not the building — it is the host, or the neighbourhood, or the gap between the photographs and the room.
Faq.listingYourHouseQuestion: Can I list my own house?
Faq.listingYourHouseAnswer: You can apply, and we read every application. We look for houses with a point of view and hosts who actually want guests rather than yield. Expect a conversation, then a visit. The whole process takes about six weeks.
Faq.contactBody: Specialists are available seven days a week, 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM Central European Time. Most questions are answered the same hour.
